rows:
HOW TO USE THIS DOCUMENT IN OTHER PROJECT CHATS
Use the stable checklist number and title. Example: "Pull up CHECKLIST 01 - Exact Stat Growth Algorithm. This chat will finish that checklist."
Each checklist is deliberately self-contained. The new chat should treat already-locked Pokemon project canon as fixed unless the checklist explicitly requires a new decision.
When a checklist is completed, its decisions should be recorded back into the relevant canonical gameplay / design data rather than creating a competing rule set.

blocks.text: Stable reference names: CHECKLIST 01 through CHECKLIST 17
Use these exact identifiers when referring to a checklist in another chat.
Purpose: Lock how canonical base stats become Fire Emblem-style growth percentages.
Reference prompt: "Pull up CHECKLIST 01 - Exact Stat Growth Algorithm. This chat will finish this checklist."
[ ] Define the mathematical conversion from each species' six base stats into HP, Attack, Defence, Special Attack, Special Defence and Speed growth percentages.
[ ] Decide whether BST itself modifies overall growth quality or only the distribution between the six stats.
[ ] Establish the minimum possible growth percentage.
[ ] Establish the maximum possible growth percentage.
[ ] Confirm every level performs six independent growth rolls.
[ ] Define the successful growth increment for normal stats.
[ ] Decide whether HP also gains +1 per successful roll or uses a different increment.
[ ] Confirm failed rolls produce no increase.
[ ] Decide whether a level can produce zero successful growths.
[ ] Decide whether a level can produce all six successful growths.
[ ] Decide whether any bad-luck protection exists.
[ ] Decide whether any exceptional-growth mechanic exists.
[ ] Confirm higher-level generated monsters simulate all prior growth rolls from their fixed seed.
[ ] Confirm reloading cannot reroll historical growth.
[ ] Confirm evolution does not reroll historical growth.
[ ] Validate expected Level 50 and Level 100 stat distributions.
[ ] Add final growth percentages to the canonical species data.
Purpose: Create the complete authored wild-monster distribution for the world.
Reference prompt: "Pull up CHECKLIST 02 - Route & Destination Encounter Tables. This chat will finish this checklist."
[ ] List every location where random encounters can occur.
[ ] List every major route, minor path, forest, cave, ruin, dungeon, Hell encounter area and optional/postgame area.
[ ] Assign each encounter-enabled location its own encounter table.
[ ] Assign species percentages to every table.
[ ] Give each species a minimum encounter level.
[ ] Give each species a maximum encounter level.
[ ] Define extremely rare encounters if required.
[ ] Determine whether some monsters require particular terrain.
[ ] Determine whether some monsters require a particular story state.
[ ] Determine whether some monsters require a special interaction.
[ ] Determine whether some monsters require a hidden area.
[ ] Identify fossil acquisition separately from ordinary encounters.
[ ] Decide whether encounter terrain is visually marked.
[ ] Decide whether caves use step-based encounters throughout.
[ ] Ensure early routes cannot generate unreasonable lethal spikes.
[ ] Ensure later routes naturally become poor grinding locations through level-gap XP scaling.
[ ] Confirm there is no dynamic monster-level scaling.
Purpose: Establish the navigable world before finished city/map artwork.
Reference prompt: "Pull up CHECKLIST 03 - World Progression & Functional Map Structure. This chat will finish this checklist."

[ ] Decide how returning to earlier towns operates.
[ ] Decide when restoration versions of towns replace conquest versions.
[ ] Establish the expected critical path through the whole game.
Purpose: Create every combat-capable human opponent and appropriate AI/team progression.

[ ] Determine whether trainer class affects monster preferences.

[ ] Build trainers for each midgame route.
[ ] Build trainers for each late-game route.
[ ] Define the expected level curve by chapter.
[ ] Assign every trainer a team size, monster species, levels, abilities, legal moves and held items if used.
[ ] Build Pate's team at every encounter.
[ ] Build Trade's team at every encounter.
[ ] Build all eight mortal leader teams.
[ ] Make each Warden team exploit its terrain.
[ ] Decide which AI tiers switch monsters.
[ ] Decide which AI tiers use healing items.
[ ] Decide which AI tiers predict type matchups.
[ ] Decide which AI tiers use setup / status tactics.
Purpose: Finalise the eight Warden battlefield conditions and teams built around them.
Reference prompt: "Pull up CHECKLIST 05 - Hell Terrain Finalisation. This chat will finish this checklist."
[ ] Ossael: confirm sandstorm-style damage and immunities.

[ ] Nema: build the Dark / Ghost team.
[ ] Determine whether Warden terrain lasts indefinitely.
[ ] Decide whether player moves can remove or replace Warden terrain.

[ ] Decide whether the Warden terrain resumes after a replacement expires.
[ ] Ensure every terrain uses the normal readable battle UI.
Purpose: Build the entire non-monster inventory and economic system.
Reference prompt: "Pull up CHECKLIST 06 - Items, Shops & Economy. This chat will finish this checklist."

Purpose: Fully specify death recording and costly resurrection.
Reference prompt: "Pull up CHECKLIST 07 - Memorial & Resurrection System. This chat will finish this checklist."
[ ] Define when the Civeton memorial becomes available.
[ ] Record current / former moves as required.
[ ] Decide whether flavour epitaphs are generated.

Reference prompt: "Pull up CHECKLIST 08 - Party & Reserve Management. This chat will finish this checklist."

[ ] Decide whether reserve access is restricted in hostile areas.
[ ] Determine behaviour when the active party has no living monsters.
[ ] Determine behaviour if the reserve contains living monsters during a wipe.
[ ] Decide whether the player must manually retrieve reserve replacements after losses.
[ ] Handle permanent deletion cleanly when a party member dies.
Purpose: Fully separate battle defeat from human death.
Reference prompt: "Pull up CHECKLIST 09 - Leader & Trainer Fate System. This chat will finish this checklist."
[ ] Identify every battle requiring post-battle fate resolution.
[ ] Identify all eight leader fate scenes.
[ ] Define special authored exceptions where applicable.
[ ] Ensure monster-party defeat alone never automatically kills a human.
[ ] Decide whether every important opponent is physically captured first.
[ ] Autosave immediately after a fate decision.
[ ] Create one state value / flag per leader fate.
[ ] Mark executed characters eligible to appear in Hell.
[ ] Mark spared characters eligible for restoration / postgame appearances.
[ ] Ensure neither option simply gives superior mechanical rewards.
[ ] Define Aimon / player defeat outcomes in scripted major battles.
[ ] Define story-controlled cases where an enemy chooses to spare the player.
Purpose: Convert the narrative Bible into implementation-ready game state.
Reference prompt: "Pull up CHECKLIST 10 - Story Event & Flag Master List. This chat will finish this checklist."
[ ] Establish a naming convention for flags.
[ ] Create unique evolution-item acquisition flags where required.
[ ] Define mutually exclusive state variables where appropriate.
[ ] Create the master event-ID naming convention.
[ ] Map Story Bible scenes to event IDs.
[ ] Produce the implementation-ready event / flag table.
Purpose: Perform the final balance and logic pass over all 187 monsters' evolution rules.
Reference prompt: "Pull up CHECKLIST 11 - Evolution Validation. This chat will finish this checklist."
[ ] Check first evolution levels against BST increases.
[ ] Check final evolution levels against BST increases.
[ ] Ensure strong final forms arrive later.
[ ] Ensure weaker ordinary forms evolve reasonably early.
[ ] Ensure each item theme matches the transformation.
[ ] Ensure each item appears before evolution would reasonably be desired.
[ ] Ensure renewable item sources exist where appropriate.
[ ] Tie every story flag to a specific actual scene.
[ ] Decide what happens if a monster is obtained after the triggering story decision.
[ ] Decide what happens if a monster passes minimum evolution level before receiving the trigger.
[ ] Confirm each promotion uses target base stat minus source base stat.
[ ] Check unusual cases where a target base stat is lower.
[ ] Decide whether negative promotion deltas are allowed.
[ ] Confirm evolved growth weights switch immediately.
Purpose: Balance and validate the individual learnsets already created for all 187 species.
Reference prompt: "Pull up CHECKLIST 12 - Learnset Validation. This chat will finish this checklist."
[ ] Check every species has a legal learnset.
[ ] Check every move exists in the 354-move catalogue.
[ ] Check every monster receives usable early offence.
[ ] Ensure every monster receives STAB reasonably early.
[ ] Ensure both types receive useful moves where appropriate.
[ ] Check physical attackers receive appropriate physical moves.
[ ] Check special attackers receive appropriate special moves.
[ ] Check defensive monsters receive support moves.
[ ] Check fast monsters receive suitable utility / priority where appropriate.
[ ] Prevent high-power moves from appearing too early.
[ ] Prevent excessively weak moves from remaining too late.
[ ] Ensure signature moves arrive at sensible levels / evolution points.
[ ] Verify every planned trainer's moves are legal at their battle level.
[ ] Finalise all 187 learnsets as implementation data.
Purpose: Decide exactly what the battle engine does in every awkward scenario.
Reference prompt: "Pull up CHECKLIST 13 - Battle Edge Cases. This chat will finish this checklist."
[ ] Starter reaches 0 HP with two lives remaining.
[ ] Starter reaches 0 HP with one life remaining.
[ ] Both active monsters reach 0 HP simultaneously.
[ ] Switch when only one living monster remains.
[ ] Capture final enemy in a wild encounter.
[ ] Attempt capture on a trainer-owned monster.
[ ] Attempt capture on a boss / story monster.
[ ] Learn a new move after battle.
[ ] Autosave ordering for all battle-end consequences.

Reference prompt: "Pull up CHECKLIST 14 - Starter Three-Life System. This chat will finish this checklist."

[ ] Decide whether the starter can be revived during that same battle.

[ ] Decide post-battle status after a non-final life loss.
[ ] Decide whether alchemist treatment is required.
[ ] Display lives clearly in the summary screen.
[ ] Decide whether lives appear during battle.
[ ] Decide whether life losses are stored in memorial history.
[ ] Decide whether lost starter lives can ever be restored.
[ ] Decide whether starter resurrection after final death uses ordinary memorial rules.
[ ] Define Pate's dynamically assigned starter lives.
[ ] Define Trade's dynamically assigned starter lives.
[ ] Handle starter evolution while lives are already lost.
